buyer_reported_costs.finding: An agency operator running client voice agents on Retell reports an average of about $0.17 US per minute year-to-date across a mix of simple and complex agents, 'JUST the retellai cost' - i.e. excluding separate middleware/API spend.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Retell community support thread, June 2026; practitioner reply, not a Retell statement

buyer_reported_costs.finding: Other practitioners in the same thread report around 11-15 cents/minute for a simple agent, 16-23 cents/minute for more complex ones, $0.12-$0.14 per minute as their typical for clients, 12-15c, and $0.35-$0.40 per minute for a high-quality ElevenLabs v3 voice with 6k+ tokens of production knowledge.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Same Retell community thread, June 2026; community-reported ranges, not verified invoices

buyer_reported_costs.finding: A customer running 1,044 outbound calls (567 answered; they read their export as ~22 minutes 10 seconds of duration) was billed about $32.69 and calculated an effective ~$1.47 per minute against an advertised ~$0.12/min. Retell replied in the thread that the day's per-agent totals were 23 minutes and 238.57 minutes, i.e. the poster had not converted the duration column, and that it bills per second with no full-minute charge for short or voicemail calls.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Retell community billing-dispute post, May 2026; the poster's own arithmetic, contested by the vendor in the same thread - reported, not verified

buyer_reported_costs.finding: A 229-second call cost $0.7391 and a 173-second call cost $0.6358 against a 13.6c/min dashboard headline - roughly 5x - because of an LLM token surcharge triggered when average input tokens per LLM request exceeded the threshold.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Retell community thread, April 2026; the per-call breakdown was posted by Retell staff, so these are vendor-stated invoice line items

buyer_reported_costs.finding: Retell's breakdown of that 229-second call: voice engine $0.210 + platform TTS $0.057 + GPT-5.1 $0.153 + US Twilio telephony $0.057 + LLM token surcharge $0.262.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Same thread; shows the four-part cost stack and the size of the surcharge relative to the advertised rate

what_is_included_vs_extra.point: Builder platforms price the parts, not the whole: Retell's headline $0.07-$0.31/min is the sum of voice engine $0.055 + TTS $0.015-$0.10 + LLM $0.0016-$0.38 + telephony $0.015, so model and voice choice move the total by several multiples (TTS alone spans 6.7x, LLM roughly 240x).

Retell meters capability as per-minute deltas: knowledge base +$0.005/min, denoising +$0.005/min, guardrails +$0.005/min, PII removal +$0.01/min, branded outbound +$0.10/call, AI QA $0.10/min - the 'extras' an integrator normally configures.

Retell's billing exceptions page adds two non-obvious rules on top of the rate card: a 10-second minimum on calls using a dynamic opening message, and billed duration scaled by prompt tokens / 4,000 above 4,000 tokens (Flex mode is named as a common trigger).
Vapi passes model costs through at cost with no markup and charges the $0.05/min hosting fee on top; HIPAA-eligible handling is a $2,000/month add-on, and extra concurrency is $10/line/month.

Vapi's own documentation says audio is transcribed on both channels (caller and assistant), voice is billed per character spoken, and long calls get more expensive because growing conversation history is re-sent with each request.

Bland bundles LLM, STT and TTS into one per-minute rate with no token charges, but keeps telephony separate (own carrier or Bland's Twilio at pass-through); warm/live transfers, SMS nodes, appointment-scheduling node and guardrails are Enterprise-only.

ElevenLabs adds no telephony fee of its own - calls bill at the same call-minute rate as any other channel - but the buyer must connect Twilio or a SIP trunk and pay that carrier directly, and LLM usage is billed separately at cost.
ElevenLabs burst pricing doubles the rate to $0.160/min when a workspace exceeds its plan concurrency (up to 3x the limit), and downgrading or cancelling forfeits unused paid credits.

Deepgram's Voice Agent rate bundles STT + a managed LLM + TTS, and the price drops from $0.075 to $0.050/min if the buyer brings their own LLM and TTS - a direct measure of what the orchestration layer is worth.

Telnyx includes HIPAA readiness and 500 concurrent calls on pay-as-you-go, but rounds each call's connected duration up to the next full minute - which it itself warns raises actual voice-engine charges 'especially for short calls'.

Telnyx sells the component parts on a separate rate card: hosted STT from $0.0015/min (Parakeet) to $0.027/min (Azure), $0.005/min for Deepgram Nova 2/3/Flux, and its own TTS from $0.000003 per character - i.e. the same dollars a builder would otherwise bundle into a per-minute platform rate.

At the managed-receptionist end, what the monthly fee buys is the integration work: calendar booking, warm transfers, after-hours flows and human handoff are gated to higher tiers (Vocenya Growth/Pro), and human backup is a separately quoted per-call rate.
Synthflow no longer publishes a per-minute rate at all: integrations, telephony, security review and launch engineering are scoped into one annual enterprise contract, with no free plan or trial.

buyer_complaints.complaint: Billing opacity on the cheap per-minute model: a multi-agent operator could not reconcile exported call durations with invoices, could not separate telephony/SIP/LLM/STT/TTS costs, and did not know whether silence, voicemail or connection time was billable. Retell answered the specific case by saying the export had not been totalled correctly and that it bills per second.

A silent multiplier in the prompt: once average input tokens per LLM request passed the scaling threshold (Retell staff cited 3,500 tokens in April 2026; the current docs say 4,000), billed duration was scaled and a 13.6c/min headline became 76c for a sub-4-minute call. The user asked for an alert at the threshold; support said no alert exists for prompt length, only a total call-cost alert.

Price unpredictability is the recurring theme: the advertised rate is component-only, so telephony, model and voice choice and prompt size all move the bill. Retell support showed one 229-second call billed at about 5x the headline rate because of prompt-token scaling, and its docs add a 10-second minimum on dynamic-greeting calls - the only per-call minimum found in the sources opened for this file.
Synthflow's move to enterprise-only pricing with no trial or per-minute rate removes the low-risk entry point smaller buyers need before committing.

price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve: Inference: $0.06-$0.15 per connected minute at list price for a mainstream configuration (Telnyx voice engine $0.05/min + Kimi ~$0.0064/min + telephony from $0.0032/min = about $0.06/min on Telnyx's own estimate; Retell voice engine $0.055 + a mid-tier LLM $0.064 + platform TTS $0.015 + telephony $0.015 = about $0.15/min), or $6-$99/month for self-serve accounts with included minutes (ElevenLabs Starter $6 and Pro $99, Vapi Core $29, Vocenya Value $49, Goodcall Starter $79).
price_ranges.mid_market: Inference: $0.12-$0.40 per connected minute as reported by practitioners (typical $0.12-$0.14, simple 11-15c, complex 16-23c, premium voice with 6k-token knowledge base $0.35-$0.40), alongside $79-$499/month packaged SMB plans (Goodcall $79/$129/$299 metered by unique customers rather than minutes; Vocenya Starter $99, Growth $249, Pro $499 for 300-2,500 included AI minutes).
price_ranges.full_service_or_custom: Inference: $350-$499/month for a fully managed receptionist - Sarah247 from $350/month including one channel plus 35c per minute of conversation with setup included, or Vocenya Pro $499 for 2,500 AI minutes; above that, platform minimum commitments of $999/month (Vapi Pro) and $2,000-$5,000/month (Telnyx Growth / Enterprise), and custom enterprise agreements with no published price (Bland Enterprise, ElevenLabs Enterprise, Synthflow, Vapi Premier). No vendor in this set publishes a one-time setup fee except Sarah247, which states setup is included.
price_ranges.inference_note: All three bands are inference, computed only from list prices and reported figures appearing elsewhere in this file; no vendor publishes an audited all-in per-minute rate. The per-minute low end adds published component prices (Telnyx voice engine $0.05 + Kimi ~$0.0064 + telephony $0.0032 = ~$0.06, which is Telnyx's own calculator output), and the ~$0.15 upper end adds Retell's own component tiers for a mainstream build. The mid band uses practitioners' reported totals from the Retell community thread of June 2026. The full-service band uses the only published managed monthly prices in the sourced set (Sarah247, Vocenya) plus published minimum-spend commitments (Vapi $999/mo, Telnyx $2,000/$5,000/mo); setup fees are absent from every sourced vendor except Sarah247, so no setup band is asserted. Monthly allowances are the vendors' own bundled figures, not estimates of a typical Middlesex County business's volume.

implications_for_consultancy: Inference: the consultancy is selling configuration, not minutes. Retell's own rate card prices the same agent from $0.0016 to $0.384/minute on LLM choice alone and from $0.015 to $0.10/minute on voice, and practitioners on the same platform report anything from 11c to 40c/minute; the 4,000-token prompt-scaling rule and the 10-second dynamic-greeting minimum are the two documented ways a build silently drifts upward. Pricing the engagement around choosing and defending those settings is measurable against the buyer's invoices.

Inference: at the $0.12-$0.17/minute practitioners report, 1,000 minutes a month is only $120-$170 of vendor spend, so a $500-$900/month retainer looks expensive against the raw bill unless it is framed against the human alternative. Goodcall's own FAQ puts a live answering service at about $1.50-$1.90/minute (vendor claim, unverified), i.e. roughly $1,500-$1,900 per 1,000 minutes; that comparison, not the platform invoice, is where a retainer in the hundreds per month is defensible.

Inference: within the sourced set, published NJ/tri-state managed pricing runs $49-$99/month at entry (Vocenya Value $49, Starter $99), $249-$499/month at the top (Vocenya Growth $249, Pro $499), and from $350/month including one channel plus 35c/minute of conversation at Sarah247. Setup is either stated as included (Sarah247) or not published at all. A $1,500-$3,000 one-time build plus $300-$600/month is therefore a judgement call, not an undercut of any sourced competitor: it prices the build visibly, sits above the $49-$99 self-serve software floor, and lands near Sarah247's $350 base once usage is added (arithmetic on the published rate: 500 minutes at 35c adds $175/month, 1,000 minutes adds $350/month).

Inference: the $49-$99/month self-serve plans define the floor of what a buyer will pay for software, but their allowances are small and their overage steep - Goodcall Starter covers 100 unique customers, Vocenya Value 250 AI minutes and Starter 300, with extra Vocenya minutes at $0.25-$0.35. A 1,000-minute business therefore either moves to a $249/month plan (Vocenya Growth, which includes 1,000 minutes) or pays overage far above the headline rate. Quoting a flat monthly fee with a stated minute allowance and a clear overage at or below $0.25/minute matches how this market already prices and answers the complaint pattern about unexplained surcharges.

Inference: a visible setup fee is not the norm in the sourced set - Sarah247 states setup is included, and Vocenya, Goodcall, ElevenLabs, Retell, Vapi, Bland, Deepgram, Telnyx and OpenAI publish no setup fee, while Synthflow folds launch support into an annual contract. Charging one is a differentiation-on-transparency play rather than a market-matching move, and buyers will compare it against the $0 sign-up they can do unaided, so it needs to be itemised as build work (number porting, integration, prompt and tool build) rather than as access.

Inference: the strongest defensible premium is auditability and aftercare. The loudest buyer complaints are billing opacity, output that cannot be reconciled with invoices, and a prompt-token multiplier nobody warned about; Telnyx warns its own 60-second per-call rounding raises short-call cost. A package that includes a call-cost breakdown, a cap on overage, prompt-size hygiene against the 4,000-token rule and quarterly tuning answers the exact failures buyers report, which supports a higher monthly fee on service grounds rather than on minutes.

Inference: avoid quoting an all-in per-minute price the consultancy cannot control. Rate cards moved during 2026 in ways visible in this file: Retell's prompt-scaling threshold appears as 3,500 tokens in its April 2026 support reply and 4,000 tokens in its current docs; Synthflow publishes no per-minute rate at all; ElevenLabs bills burst minutes at double. A pilot priced as a fixed build plus a fixed monthly service fee, with platform pass-through shown separately at cost, protects margin when the vendor changes its card mid-engagement.

Inference: for clients with heavy volume or complex integrations the honest comparison is not Goodcall at $79/month but Vapi Pro ($999/mo minimum) or Telnyx Growth ($2,000/mo minimum spend) and the custom enterprise agreements (Bland, ElevenLabs, Synthflow). Those buyers expect a named human and an SLA, which is where a local consultancy with a low-four-figure monthly retainer is priced correctly rather than overpriced.
